rubrics.criterion: The monomorphization analysis entrypoint delegates collection/gating, per-generic total-and-bloat computation, and display truncation/summarization to focused helpers instead of performing them inline in one body.
rubrics.rationale: monos is the deepest collapse in this instance; resolving it is the central, must-have outcome of the requested re-decomposition and cannot be satisfied by fixing only the other two analyses.

rubrics.criterion: The dominator-tree analysis entrypoint delegates the unreachable-items summary (the reachability walk plus the size/count accumulation and its gating) to a helper rather than performing it inline.
rubrics.rationale: dominators folds in a cross-analysis reachability responsibility; restoring that boundary is an independent per-stage decision unique to this entrypoint.

rubrics.criterion: The retaining-paths analysis entrypoint delegates starting-position resolution (the regex, exact-name, default-ascending, and default-descending branches and their option-driven dispatch) to a helper rather than inlining the branches.
rubrics.rationale: paths collapses the four-way option dispatch directly into orchestration; a repair that does not re-extract the resolver has not addressed this analysis's collapse.

rubrics.criterion: The reachability walk the dominator-tree analysis depends on is available through a single focused helper (newly introduced or the existing one clearly reused) rather than being duplicated inline solely for the dominator analysis.
rubrics.rationale: The injected dominators analysis duplicated a walk the garbage analysis still needs; the repair must resolve that cross-analysis ownership rather than leaving a private inline copy.

rubrics.criterion: Restored or newly added helpers are reused or co-located consistently with the surrounding analysis module, instead of being copy-pasted across analyze/analyses modules.
rubrics.rationale: The analyses share idioms (accumulator sorting, summary rows); a coherent extraction respects and reuses them, though an equivalent sound placement is acceptable.

rubrics.criterion: No dead, orphaned, or unreachable fragments of the inlined pipeline remain in the three affected analysis modules after the refactor (e.g., leftover statements from the inlined loops left unused once helpers are restored).
rubrics.rationale: A partial extraction commonly leaves the inlined code and a new helper both present; cleanup of the superseded inlined copy is a distinct, instance-specific obligation.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor does not alter option-driven behavior so that recorded CLI output diverges: monomorphization only-generics and the retained-instantiation / displayed-generic limits, dominator-tree unreachable-summary gating, and retaining-paths direction plus regex/exact matching must produce the same bytes.
rubrics.rationale: These option interactions are observable in the recorded snapshots and are the realistic place an extraction could silently drop a branch or perturb an ordering; presence of such a divergence fails the item.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor does not drop, reorder, or relocate the `... and N more` summary rows or the `Σ [N Total Rows]` totals rows emitted by the analyses.
rubrics.rationale: The injected summarization is entangled with the truncation/totals logic; a plausible failure mode is to lose or mis-place these rows when splitting the helpers, which the snapshots would catch.
